lesson.title: First Impressions: Introducing Yourself Professionally
lesson.content:
Welcome to English class! In SMK, English is not just a subject; it's a **global tool** for your future career. Our first lesson is about **Self-Introduction**. Imagine you are in a job interview or meeting a new client. How do you introduce yourself? You should mention your name, your expertise (your major in SMK), and your passion. For example: 'Hello, I am Budi. I am a student majoring in Computer and Network Engineering. I am passionate about cybersecurity.'

We will learn formal greetings like 'Good morning,' 'Pleasured to meet you,' and 'How do you do?' (used for the very first time meeting someone). Remember, a professional introduction is clear, concise, and confident. Use active verbs to describe your skills. Your introduction is your 'elevator pitch'—a short speech that tells people who you are and what you can do. Let's make sure your first impression is a great one!

Practice introducing yourself in front of a mirror or with a friend. Pay attention to your body language and eye contact. Being able to introduce yourself in English opens many doors to international opportunities. You are not just a student; you are a future professional. Let's start this journey with confidence and a big smile. Welcome to the world of professional English!

lesson.title: Networking 101: Introducing Others and Small Talk
lesson.content:
In a workplace, you often need to introduce your colleagues or boss to someone else. This is called **Introducing Others**. You can use phrases like: 'I would like to introduce you to...', 'This is my supervisor, Mr. Tanaka,' or 'Have you met our lead engineer, Sarah?'. This skill helps you build a strong professional network. Besides introductions, we also learn **Small Talk**—light conversation to break the ice, such as talking about the weather, current industry trends, or work projects.

Small talk is not just 'useless talk'; it builds **rapport** and trust with others. Avoid sensitive topics like politics or religion in professional small talk. Instead, ask open-ended questions like: 'How do you find working in this industry?' or 'What do you think about the new technology we are using?'. Listening is just as important as speaking. By being a good conversationalist, you show that you are approachable and professional. Let's practice these social skills to boost your career!

Good networking starts with a simple 'hello' and a genuine interest in others. Don't be afraid to make mistakes; what matters is your willingness to communicate. English is the bridge that connects you to people from different backgrounds. Master the art of introduction and small talk, and you will find it much easier to collaborate in any international environment. Happy networking!

lesson.title: Who's Who: Describing People in the Workplace
lesson.content:
Sometimes you need to describe a person to help someone find them or to give a recommendation. In this lesson, we learn adjectives to describe **Physical Appearance** (tall, slim, wearing glasses) and **Personality/Traits** (diligent, creative, organized, reliable). For example: 'Our manager is a very organized and disciplined person. She has short black hair and always wears a blue blazer.' This helps in creating clear communication in a busy work environment.

We use the 'Simple Present Tense' with the verb 'to be' and 'have/has' for descriptions. Beyond physical looks, focus on **Professional Qualities**. Is your teammate 'cooperative'? Is your technician 'punctual'? These words are very useful when writing a performance review or an employee recommendation. Learning how to describe people accurately shows your attention to detail. Let's expand your vocabulary to describe your future colleagues and role models effectively.

Try to describe one of your teachers or a famous professional in your field using at least five adjectives. Remember to use polite language. Describing people is about more than just words; it's about observing and appreciating the diversity of individuals you will work with. The better you can describe others, the better you can communicate roles and responsibilities in your team. Keep practicing your descriptive skills!

lesson.title: My Workplace: Describing Facilities and Locations
lesson.content:
Can you describe your school or your future workplace? In this lesson, we focus on **Describing Places**. You will learn words related to facilities like 'workshop,' 'laboratory,' 'warehouse,' 'office,' and 'canteen.' Use prepositions of place such as 'next to,' 'between,' 'on the second floor,' and 'opposite to.' For example: 'The chemistry lab is located on the first floor, next to the library. It is spacious and well-equipped.'

Describing your workplace is important for giving directions or explaining your company's capabilities to visitors. Use adjectives like 'modern,' 'clean,' 'crowded,' 'peaceful,' or 'strategic.' Knowing how to describe the layout of a building is a vital skill, especially for those in construction, architecture, or hospitality majors. It ensures everyone knows where to go and what to expect. Let's learn to describe your environment with precision and clarity.

Think about your favorite place at school. Describe it in three sentences. Mention where it is, what it looks like, and what you can do there. Clear descriptions of places help in organizing work logistics and ensuring safety. If you can explain where the emergency exit or the main server room is in English, you are already one step ahead in being a responsible and professional worker. Let's explore your world through English!

lesson.title: Tools of the Trade: Describing Equipment and Function
lesson.content:
As an SMK student, you deal with many tools every day. In this lesson, we learn to describe **Objects**, especially tools and machinery. You need to mention the name, shape, color, material, and most importantly, the **Function**. Use phrases like 'It is used for...', 'It is made of...', and 'Its purpose is to...'. For example: 'A digital multimeter is a tool used for measuring voltage, current, and resistance. It is usually made of plastic and has a small LCD screen.'

Accuracy is key here. If you describe a tool incorrectly, it could lead to work errors or accidents. Learn the difference between 'heavy-duty,' 'portable,' 'automatic,' and 'manual.' This vocabulary is essential for reading technical manuals or ordering supplies from international vendors. Describing objects also helps you in marketing products if you are in business or entrepreneurship. Every object has a story and a purpose; let's learn how to tell that story in English.

Choose one tool from your major's workshop. Write a short description including its appearance and what it does. By mastering this, you will be able to explain technical concepts to non-experts or international partners easily. English for technical purposes is your 'superpower' in the global job market. Let's dive deep into the details of the tools that will build your future career!

lesson.title: Attention Please! Workplace Announcements
lesson.content:
In a professional setting, information is often shared through **Announcements**. An announcement must be clear and answer the 5W+1H questions: Who, What, Where, When, Why, and How. In this lesson, you will learn the structure of an announcement: Heading/Title, Content (the main information), and Closing (who to contact). Common topics include office meetings, holiday schedules, safety drills, or new company policies.

When writing an announcement, use a direct and formal tone. For example: 'To all staff, please be informed that there will be a fire safety drill this Friday at 10 AM. Attendance is mandatory.' Pay attention to keywords like 'mandatory,' 'postponed,' 'cancelled,' and 'scheduled.' Being able to understand and write announcements ensures that you are always up-to-date and compliant with workplace rules. Communication is the lifeblood of any organization.

Try to write a short announcement for your class about an upcoming school event. Make sure the date and time are clearly stated. Announcements are meant to be noticed and understood quickly. In the digital age, announcements are often sent via email or messaging apps. Mastering this skill will make you a more effective communicator in any team. Let's get the message across clearly and professionally!

lesson.title: What Happened? Sharing Past Experiences
lesson.content:
A **Recount Text** tells about past events or experiences. It follows a chronological order: Orientation (who, where, when), Events (what happened in sequence), and Re-orientation (your feeling or summary). In SMK, recount texts are very useful for writing **Work Reports** or explaining your internship experience. You use the 'Simple Past Tense' (V2) like 'visited,' 'repaired,' 'installed,' and 'learned.' For example: 'Last month, I did my internship at a local car workshop.'

By telling your story, you share valuable lessons and progress. You can use time connectors like 'First,' 'Then,' 'After that,' and 'Finally' to make your story flow smoothly. Recounting your achievements in English is also a great way to build your portfolio. It shows that you can reflect on your work and learn from your actions. Whether it's a successful project or a mistake you've corrected, every experience is a stepping stone to your success.

Write a short paragraph about what you did in your workshop last week. Use the simple past tense correctly. Being able to report 'what happened' clearly is a highly valued skill in any industry. It helps in troubleshooting problems and documenting progress. Let's learn from the past to build a better future. Your story matters, so let's learn how to tell it well in English!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Legends and Fables with Moral Lessons

lesson.title: Story Time: Narrative and Moral Values
lesson.content:
A **Narrative Text** is a story with a complication or problem that needs to be solved. The structure is: Orientation, Complication, Resolution, and Coda (moral lesson). We learn through stories like legends, fables, and myths. Why do we study this in SMK? Because narratives teach us about **culture, creativity, and ethics**. Many international companies value employees who can think creatively and understand different cultural perspectives.

Narratives often use descriptive language and dialogue to make the story come alive. They also teach us important moral values like honesty, hard work, and teamwork—qualities that are essential in the professional world. For example, the story of 'The Tortoise and the Hare' teaches us that 'slow and steady wins the race.' In your career, consistency and persistence are often more important than just being fast. Let's enjoy the beauty of storytelling while learning life lessons.

Think of a local legend from your area. Can you tell the core story in three English sentences? Practicing narrative skills improves your vocabulary and your ability to engage an audience. It's also a great way to improve your pronunciation through storytelling. Every culture has its unique stories; by sharing them in English, you become a cultural ambassador for Indonesia. Let's learn, enjoy, and grow through stories!

lesson.title: Visit Indonesia: Describing Tourist Attractions
lesson.content:
Indonesia is a beautiful country with many famous landmarks. In this lesson, we learn to write **Descriptive Texts** about tourist attractions like Borobudur Temple, Raja Ampat, or Mount Bromo. You will use adjectives like 'magnificent,' 'breathtaking,' 'historical,' and 'exotic.' For example: 'Borobudur is the largest Buddhist temple in the world, located in Magelang, Central Java. It is famous for its beautiful relief and stupas.'

This skill is particularly important for students in Tourism, Hospitality, and Culinary majors. You need to be able to promote Indonesian beauty to international tourists. Use the 'Simple Present Tense' to describe facts and characteristics. A good description makes the reader feel as if they are actually there. By promoting our local tourism, you contribute to our national economy. English is the key to welcoming the world to our beautiful islands.

Choose one tourist spot in your city. Write three sentences describing why people should visit it. Clear and attractive descriptions are powerful tools for marketing. Whether you are describing a place, a product, or a service, your goal is to make it sound appealing and interesting. Let's use our English skills to showcase the best of Indonesia to the world!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Writing Formal and Informal Business Emails

lesson.title: Digital Communication: Writing Professional Emails
lesson.content:
In the modern workplace, **Emails** and **Memos** are the primary ways to communicate. An email should have a clear 'Subject Line,' a 'Salutation' (Dear Sir/Madam), 'Opening,' 'Main Content,' 'Closing,' and 'Sign-off' (Sincerely, Best regards). In this lesson, we learn the difference between formal and informal emails. You wouldn't send the same email to your friend as you would to your manager. Tone and etiquette are very important.

We will learn common phrases like: 'I am writing to inform you that...', 'Please find the attached file,' and 'I look forward to hearing from you soon.' For those in Office Management or Business, this is a core skill. Even for technicians, you need to email reports to your clients. A well-written email shows that you are professional, respectful, and efficient. It prevents misunderstandings and builds a good reputation. Let's master the art of digital professional communication.

Try to write a short email to a teacher asking for permission to be absent. Remember to state the reason clearly and use a polite closing. In your future career, your ability to write clear emails will save time and increase productivity. English makes you globally reachable. Let's learn to communicate effectively across screens and borders!

lesson.title: Vocational English: Tools and Equipment
lesson.content:
Let's expand your **Technical Vocabulary**. Every industry has its own 'jargon' or special words. In this lesson, we learn the English names for common tools across various SMK majors: 'wrench,' 'screwdriver,' 'stethoscope,' 'whisk,' 'camera tripod,' 'router,' etc. You will also learn 'action verbs' related to these tools like 'tighten,' 'loosen,' 'measure,' 'mix,' 'record,' and 'configure.' Knowing the right word for the right tool is the first step to becoming an expert.

We will use these words in sentences like: 'Use a wrench to tighten the bolt,' or 'Configure the router to set up the network.' If you can read the English labels on your equipment, you can avoid many mistakes. Most high-tech machines come with English manuals. By mastering this vocabulary, you are preparing yourself to work in international companies or to use imported technology. Don't just know how to use the tool; know what it's called in the international language of industry.

Make a list of 10 tools you use in your major and find their English names. Use them in short sentences. Vocabulary is the building block of communication. The more specific your words, the more professional you sound. Let's build a strong foundation of vocational English today to support your technical skills tomorrow!

lesson.title: Safety First: Understanding Signs and Warnings
lesson.content:
Workplace safety is the most important rule in any industry. In this lesson, we learn about **Safety Signs** and **Instructions** in English. You will see signs like 'Caution: Wet Floor,' 'Wear Protective Gear,' 'High Voltage,' and 'Emergency Exit.' We use 'Imperative Sentences' for instructions: 'Do not enter,' 'Wear your helmet,' 'Wash your hands.' Following these signs can save lives and prevent injuries.

We will also learn how to explain safety procedures. For example: 'In case of fire, do not use the elevator. Use the stairs instead.' For students in Engineering, Mining, or Health majors, this is absolutely critical. Most international safety standards (like ISO or OHSAS) are written in English. Being 'Safety Conscious' in English makes you a highly responsible and valuable worker. Let's learn to stay safe and keep others safe by understanding the universal language of safety.

Draw three common safety signs and write their meanings in English. Safety is not just about rules; it's about a culture of care. By mastering safety English, you show that you respect yourself, your colleagues, and your workplace environment. Let's make safety a habit and a priority in every workshop and laboratory!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Directing Visitors in a Company or Hotel

lesson.title: Which Way? Giving Clear Directions
lesson.content:
Imagine a foreign visitor arrives at your office or hotel and asks for the restroom or the meeting room. How do you help them? In this lesson, we learn how to **Give Directions**. Use phrases like 'Go straight,' 'Turn left/right,' 'It's on your right hand side,' 'Go up to the second floor,' and 'It's at the end of the hallway.' Being helpful and clear is a sign of great **Customer Service**.

We also learn how to use 'Signposts' to make directions easier to follow: 'First, walk past the reception desk. Second, turn left at the corner.' For Hospitality and Tourism students, this is a daily task. For others, it's a great way to show hospitality to international guests or supervisors. Good directions prevent people from getting lost and make them feel welcome. Let's practice being a friendly and helpful guide in English.

Draw a simple map of your school and write directions from the gate to your classroom. Use at least five different direction phrases. Providing directions is a test of your spatial awareness and your ability to use prepositions correctly. It's a practical skill that you will use in many real-life situations. Let's lead the way with clear and confident English!

lesson.title: Hello, This is...: Professional Phone Etiquette
lesson.content:
Talking on the phone in English can be scary because you can't see the other person's face. In this lesson, we learn **Phone Etiquette**. You will learn how to answer the phone: 'Good morning, [Company Name], Budi speaking. How can I help you?'. You also learn how to ask who is calling: 'May I ask who's calling, please?'. And how to take a message: 'I'm sorry, he's in a meeting right now. Would you like to leave a message?'.

Speaking clearly and politely on the phone is a very important skill for administrative and service roles. We use phrases like 'Could you repeat that, please?' if we don't hear clearly, and 'Could you spell your name, please?' for accuracy. Avoid using slang on a professional call. Phone calls are often the first point of contact for a customer with a business. Let's make sure that contact is positive and professional through your excellent English phone skills.

Practice a short phone conversation with a friend. One person is the receptionist, and the other is a caller who wants to make an appointment. Being able to handle a phone call in English shows that you have high communication competence. It builds your confidence and makes you ready for an office environment. Pick up the phone and let's start talking!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Asking for Help and Permission at Work

lesson.title: Could You Help Me? Making Polite Requests
lesson.content:
In a workplace, we often need to ask for help or permission. We use **Polite Requests** with modal verbs like 'Could,' 'Would,' and 'May.' For example: 'Could you please help me move this box?', 'Would you mind checking this report?', or 'May I borrow your screwdriver for a moment?'. Using 'Please' and 'Thank you' is not just being nice; it's being professional and respectful to your team.

We also learn how to respond to requests: 'Sure, I'd be happy to,' 'Of course,' or 'I'm sorry, I'm busy right now, but I can help you later.' For students in all majors, being able to collaborate and ask for assistance politely is key to a smooth workflow. No one can do everything alone. By making polite requests, you build a supportive work environment where everyone feels respected and valued.

Write three polite requests that you might use in your workshop or lab. Remember to use 'Could' or 'Would you mind... -ing'. A polite request is much more likely to be granted than a demand. Your attitude determines your altitude in your career. Let's learn to be professional and polite in our interactions with others. How can I help you today?

lesson.title: I Think So: Expressing Opinions and Agreement
lesson.content:
In meetings or group projects, you will be asked for your **Opinion**. We use phrases like 'In my opinion...', 'I think...', or 'From my point of view...'. You also need to learn how to **Agree** ('I totally agree with you,' 'That's a great idea') or **Disagree politely** ('I see your point, but...', 'I'm afraid I don't agree'). Disagreeing without being rude is a very important soft skill in the workplace.

For example, if a teammate suggests a new way to fix a machine, you can say: 'I think that's a good idea, it might save time.' Or 'I'm not sure about that, because it might be dangerous.' We call this **Critical Thinking**. Being able to share your thoughts in English allows you to contribute to the growth of your company. Your voice matters, so let's learn how to express it clearly and respectfully in an international context.

Think of a topic related to your major (e.g., 'Should we use AI in graphic design?'). Write your opinion and one reason in English. Participating in discussions makes you an active and engaged professional. Don't be shy; your perspective is unique and valuable. Let's learn to debate and deliberate with class and intelligence!

lesson.title: 9 to 5: Describing Your Daily Work Routine
lesson.content:
What does a typical day look like for a technician, a chef, or a nurse? In this lesson, we learn to describe **Daily Routines** using the 'Simple Present Tense.' We use time expressions like 'usually,' 'always,' 'every morning,' and 'at noon.' For example: 'I usually start my shift at 8 AM. First, I check the inventory. Then, I prepare the ingredients for the day.' This helps in explaining your job description to others.

Consistency in your routine builds **Efficiency**. When you describe your routine in English, you show that you are organized and have a clear understanding of your responsibilities. This is a common topic in job interviews: 'Tell me about your typical workday.' For SMK students, being able to explain your practical tasks step-by-step is a great way to demonstrate your competence. Let's turn your daily tasks into a clear and professional narrative.

Write five sentences about your daily routine at school. Start from the moment you arrive until you go home. Routine is the foundation of mastery. By mastering the language to describe your routine, you are preparing to manage your time and tasks effectively in the real world. Every day is a chance to get better at what you do and how you say it!

lesson.title: Get the Job: Basic Job Interview Preparation
lesson.content:
It's never too early to prepare for your future! In this lesson, we learn how to answer basic **Job Interview Questions**. Questions like: 'Tell me about yourself,' 'What are your strengths?', and 'Why do you want to work for this company?'. We will learn to use positive words like 'motivated,' 'hardworking,' 'quick learner,' and 'team player.' Your goal is to show the interviewer that you are the right person for the job.

When talking about your strengths, always give an example from your school or internship. For example: 'I am a hardworking person. During my internship, I never missed a deadline.' For SMK students, highlighting your **Practical Skills** is very important. You have hands-on experience that others might not have. Let's learn how to 'sell' your skills and personality effectively in English. You have the talent; now let's get the words to prove it!

Write down your two greatest strengths and an example of when you showed them. Confidence comes from preparation. By practicing your interview skills now, you will feel much more relaxed and ready when the real moment comes. Your SMK education is a valuable asset; let's learn how to communicate its value to the global world. You are ready for success!

lesson.title: Manual Guide: Reading Technical Instructions
lesson.content:
Most technology nowadays comes with a **Manual**. In this lesson, we learn to read and understand simple technical instructions. Look for keywords like 'Step 1,' 'Warning,' 'Troubleshooting,' 'Assembly,' and 'Maintenance.' We will study the language of 'Procedure' which is usually direct and uses imperative verbs: 'Connect the cable,' 'Press the power button,' 'Wait for 5 seconds.'

Understanding a manual correctly is essential for the proper use of tools and machines. It prevents damage to the equipment and ensures your safety. For IT, Engineering, and Multimedia students, reading English documentation is a must-have skill. If you can follow a technical manual in English, you can learn any new technology in the world. Let's become 'Life-long Learners' who are not afraid of thick manuals or complex instructions. English is your manual for the world.

Find a short instruction set for a device (like a phone or a toaster) and try to translate the three most important steps into your own words. Being able to simplify complex instructions shows that you truly understand the process. Let's bridge the gap between human and machine through clear English communication. Knowledge is power, and instructions are the map to that power!

lesson.title: At Your Service: Excellent Customer Communication
lesson.content:
In any industry, the customer is the priority. In this lesson, we learn how to handle **Customer Requests** and **Complaints**. Phrases like: 'I'm sorry for the inconvenience,' 'Let me check that for you,' 'I will fix it right away,' and 'Is there anything else I can help you with?'. Being patient and polite can turn a frustrated customer into a loyal one. This is especially vital for Hospitality, Culinary, and Business majors.

We learn the **HEAT** method for complaints: Hear them out, Empathize, Apologize, and Take action. Even if you work in a technical field, you still have customers (the people who use your machines or software). Good customer service English makes you a 'User-Friendly' professional. It builds trust and ensures the long-term success of your business or company. Let's learn to serve with a smile and professional words.

Roleplay a situation where a customer is unhappy with a product. How would you apologize and offer a solution in English? Soft skills like empathy and problem-solving are just as important as hard skills. By mastering customer service English, you are building a reputation for excellence. Let's treat every customer as a guest of honor!

lesson.title: Email Attachments: Sharing Your Work Digitally
lesson.content:
In the professional world, we often share files like reports, designs, or invoices. In this lesson, we learn phrases for **Email Attachments**: 'Please find the attached file for your review,' 'I have attached the document you requested,' and 'Let me know if you have trouble opening it.' You also learn how to confirm you have received something: 'I am writing to acknowledge the receipt of your email.'

Clear communication about attachments prevents missed information. For students in Multimedia, Office Administration, or IT, this is a daily task. Always make sure your files are named correctly before attaching them (e.g., 'Report_Budi_May.pdf' instead of 'doc1.pdf'). This small detail shows your professionalism and respect for the recipient's time. Let's learn to be tech-savvy and professional in every digital interaction.

Write a short email body to send a work report to your teacher. Mention that you have attached a PDF file. Digital literacy combined with English proficiency makes you a modern and competitive worker. In the global office, the distance is just an email away. Let's make every email count!

lesson.title: Work Ethics: Punctuality and Presentation
lesson.content:
What makes a person 'Professional'? It's about their habits. In this lesson, we learn about **Workplace Etiquette**, focusing on **Punctuality** (being on time) and **Dress Code** (wearing the right uniform or attire). In English, we say 'Punctuality is the soul of business.' Being late shows a lack of respect for others' time. We also learn terms for professional clothing like 'uniform,' 'safety vest,' 'business casual,' and 'formal wear.'

Your appearance and time management tell a story about your reliability. We use 'Adverbs of Frequency' like 'always,' 'never,' and 'seldom' to describe these habits. For example: 'I always arrive 10 minutes before the meeting starts.' Or 'Our company requires all staff to wear a uniform on Mondays.' Following the etiquette shows that you are proud of your profession and your school. Let's build a culture of excellence by being punctual and well-presented every day.

Discuss with your friend: Why is it important to be on time in a workshop or kitchen? Professionalism is a set of skills that can be learned. By mastering the language of etiquette, you are aligning yourself with global standards of professional behavior. Let's be the professionals that Indonesia and the world need!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Collaborating on Projects and Task Division

lesson.title: Teamwork: Collaborating and Dividing Tasks
lesson.content:
No big project is done alone. We need **Teamwork**. In this lesson, we learn how to collaborate in English. Phrases like: 'Let's work together on this,' 'Who is responsible for...?', 'I will take care of the design,' and 'Can we help each other?'. Dividing tasks clearly (Task Division) ensures that everyone knows what to do and no work is repeated. This is essential for the success of any group project in SMK.

We learn about roles in a team: 'team leader,' 'coordinator,' 'member,' and 'specialist.' Good teamwork requires good listening and clear communication. If someone is struggling, offer help: 'Do you need a hand with that?'. If someone does a good job, give praise: 'Great job, team!'. A positive team spirit makes work enjoyable and productive. Let's learn to be great team players who can communicate and cooperate in the universal language of English.

Imagine you are in a group of 3 people to build a website or cook a meal. How would you divide the tasks in English? Teamwork is a 'soft skill' that international employers value highly. By practicing collaboration in English, you are preparing to lead or join global teams. Together, we can achieve more!

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Reporting Errors and Asking for Troubleshooting

lesson.title: Houston, We Have a Problem: Reporting Errors
lesson.content:
Mistakes happen, but the key is to report them quickly and honestly. In this lesson, we learn how to **Report Problems** or errors at work. Phrases like: 'There is a problem with the machine,' 'The system is down,' 'I made a mistake in the calculation,' and 'We are running out of supplies.' Being honest about problems shows your **Integrity**. It allows the team to find a solution before the problem gets bigger.

We also learn about **Troubleshooting**—finding the cause of a problem and fixing it. You might ask: 'What seems to be the problem?', 'When did it start happening?', and 'Have you tried restarting the device?'. For technicians and IT specialists, this is your primary job. Clear communication of the problem is the first step to the solution. Let's learn to be problem-reporters and problem-solvers in English.

Think of a common problem in your major (like a broken tool or a burnt cake). How would you report it to your supervisor in English? Facing problems with confidence and a solution-oriented mindset is the mark of a true professional. Don't hide mistakes; report them, learn from them, and fix them together with your team. English is your tool for clarity in times of trouble.

subject: Bahasa Inggris
subtopic: Opening a Meeting and Following an Agenda

lesson.title: The Meeting will Come to Order: Meeting Basics
lesson.content:
Meetings are where decisions are made. In this lesson, we learn the basics of **Meetings** in English. You learn how to open a meeting: 'Thank you for coming today,' 'Let's get started,' 'The purpose of today's meeting is...'. You also learn about an **Agenda**—a list of things to be discussed. Following the agenda keeps the meeting focused and saves time. This is a vital skill for anyone aiming for a leadership position.

We will learn phrases for 'taking the floor' or asking to speak: 'May I say something?', 'If I could just add...', and 'I have a question about...'. Participation is key. Don't just sit in the meeting; contribute your ideas. Also, learn how to close a meeting: 'Thank you for your contributions,' 'We will meet again next week,' 'The meeting is adjourned.' Being professional in a meeting shows your maturity and your readiness for a high-level career.

Write a simple 3-item agenda for a class meeting. Meetings can be long and boring, but they don't have to be. With clear English and a good agenda, you can make every meeting productive and inspiring. Let's learn to lead and participate in meetings with confidence and professional grace!

lesson.title: Let's Grab Coffee: Socializing with Colleagues
lesson.content:
Work is also about building relationships. In this lesson, we learn how to **Invite Colleagues** for social activities like lunch, coffee, or a weekend outing. Phrases like: 'Would you like to join us for lunch?', 'Do you have plans for this Saturday?', and 'Let's grab a coffee after work.' Socializing outside of tasks helps in building a friendlier and more cohesive team. We call this **Team Bonding**.

You also learn how to **Accept** ('That sounds great, I'd love to!') or **Decline** an invitation politely ('I'd love to, but I have other plans. Maybe next time?'). Respecting people's boundaries is important. Friendly socializing makes the workplace a happier place to spend your time. English helps you make friends not just from your own country, but from all over the world. Let's build a global network of friends and colleagues.

Practice inviting a friend to a weekend workshop in English. Remember to be friendly and inclusive. Small social gestures can go a long way in creating a positive work culture. By being a friendly and open person, you contribute to a healthy work-life balance for yourself and others. Let's connect beyond the tasks!

lesson.title: Good Job! Giving and Receiving Feedback
lesson.content:
Feedback is a 'gift' that helps us grow. In this lesson, we learn how to give and receive **Feedback** in English. We learn about 'Positive Feedback' ('You did an excellent job on this project') and 'Constructive Criticism' ('This is a good start, but maybe you could improve the alignment'). The goal is to help each other get better, not to hurt someone's feelings. We use the 'Sandwich Method': Positive - Area for improvement - Positive.

Receiving feedback is also a skill. Instead of being defensive, say: 'Thank you for the feedback, I will work on it,' or 'Can you explain more about how I can improve?'. This shows that you have a **Growth Mindset**. Everyone, even the boss, can improve. In the international world of work, open and honest feedback is a sign of a high-performing culture. Let's learn to give praise and helpful suggestions in English to help our team reach the top.

Try to give feedback to a friend about their English introduction. Start with something they did well. Constructive feedback is the engine of progress. By being open to feedback, you accelerate your learning and your career success. Let's help each other become the best versions of ourselves!

lesson.title: Dreams and Goals: Discussing Your Future Career
lesson.content:
Where do you see yourself in five years? In this lesson, we learn to talk about **Future Plans** and **Career Goals**. We use the 'Future Tense' with 'will' and 'be going to.' For example: 'I will be a professional chef in a five-star hotel,' or 'I am going to start my own IT company after I graduate.' Sharing your dreams in English makes them feel more real and reachable globally.

Having a clear goal helps you focus your studies in SMK. You can also talk about the steps you will take to reach your goal: 'First, I will master my technical skills. Second, I will improve my English. Third, I will look for an internship in a big company.' Your career is a long journey, and English is your passport to travel that journey around the world. Let's dream big and plan smart in the language of the future.

Write down your main career goal and three steps to achieve it in English. Having a plan gives you a sense of purpose. By being able to express your aspirations, you can attract mentors and opportunities that can help you succeed. Your future is bright, and English will help you shine even brighter. Let's aim for the stars!

lesson.title: Thinking Outside the Box: Workplace Challenges
lesson.content:
The professional world is constantly changing. In this lesson, we learn about **Critical Thinking** and **Adaptability**. You might face challenges like new software, a change in company strategy, or a difficult client. Use phrases like: 'How can we improve this?', 'What are the alternatives?', and 'I am willing to learn new skills.' Being adaptable means you are ready to grow and evolve with the industry.

We will learn words like 'innovation,' 'flexibility,' 'proactive,' and 'problem-solving.' Employers value workers who don't just follow orders, but also think about how to do things better. In English, we call this 'Thinking Outside the Box.' By being a proactive and adaptable employee, you ensure your long-term success in any career path. Challenges are not obstacles; they are opportunities to show your worth and your intelligence.

Think of a problem you faced in a school project. How did you solve it? Write two sentences about it in English. Your ability to think critically and express your solutions in English will make you a standout professional in the global market. Let's embrace challenges with a positive and smart mindset. You have the power to create change!

lesson.title: Your Global Key: Final Reflections on Grade 10 English
lesson.content:
Congratulations! You have completed the Grade 10 English curriculum for SMK. You have learned how to introduce yourself, describe your workplace, read manuals, write emails, and even prepare for job interviews. The most important thing to remember is: **English is a skill, not a secret**. The more you use it, the better you get. Don't be afraid to speak; every mistake is a lesson.

In the world of industry and technology, English is the 'Operating System.' It allows you to access information, connect with international experts, and work anywhere in the world. Your SMK skills are your 'Hardware,' and English is your 'Software.' Together, they make you a powerful and successful individual. Keep practicing, keep watching English movies, reading English manuals, and listening to English songs. The world is waiting for your talents.

We hope this class has given you the confidence and the tools to start your professional journey. You are no longer just a student; you are a global citizen and a future leader in your field. Go out there and show the world what an SMK graduate can do! Good luck in Grade 11, and remember to keep your English spirit high. See you at the top! Merdeka!
